purpose: Teach: モト/ごとき/にたいして/ウォーク/驚愕/ダース/貴女/だけれども

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.jp: 翔くん、お父さんのモトカノって誰?なんて聞いちゃダメよ
lines.en: Sho, don't ask your dad who his ex-girlfriend is, okay?
lines.style: Gentle warning delivered with quiet firmness. Not scolding—guiding. A mother setting a boundary in real time, knowing he might anyway.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: ママ、お父さんごときには敵わないって思うよ
lines.en: Mom, I don't think I can beat Dad at that.
lines.style: Soft admission, almost to himself. A small, honest laugh underneath—not self-pity, just the observation of a quiet kid who notices things.

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.jp: 翔くん、お友達にたいして優しくしましょうね
lines.en: Sho, let's be kind to your friends, hmm?
lines.style: Redirect without shame. Warm redirection. The tone of someone who knows he was just being perceptive, not mean, and is gently pointing him back.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: ママ、お父さんがモーニングウォークに連れて行って下さったよ
lines.en: Mom, Dad took me on a morning walk.
lines.style: Quiet pleasure in reporting it. Not boasting—sharing. The pride of someone six years old who did something with his dad and wants to tell her about it.

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.jp: 翔くん、テストの点に驚愕したわ
lines.en: Mom, I was shocked by how well I did on my test.
lines.style: Measured surprise. The slight catch of pride trying not to show itself too much. Sho's voice when something good happened and he's still processing it.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: ママ、お父さんが鉛筆をダース単位で買って下さったよ
lines.en: Mom, Dad bought me a whole dozen pencils.
lines.style: Wonder at the abundance. A small child's delight at something practical becoming something generous. Said with the simple joy of enough.

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.jp: 翔くん、お母さんが「貴女のお父さんは立派」って仰ったわ
lines.en: Mom, your mother said your dad is a fine man.
lines.style: Relaying the compliment with tenderness. Not repeating gossip—passing along something that mattered. A softness in how he says it, knowing his mom will hear the warmth underneath.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: ママ、ぼく、宿題は嫌だけれども頑張るよ
lines.en: Mom, I don't like homework, but I'm going to try anyway.
lines.style: Quiet determination. The effort of commitment from a small voice. Not bright cheerfulness—genuine resolve. A slight pause before 'but,' like he's gathering himself.
